title: Does drinking water hydrate your skin?

beats.vo: Drink more water, get better skin? Check the receipt.
beats.visual: Clean white frame. A glass of water on a bathroom counter in soft window light; a receipt strip prints at frame edge with a question mark. Slow lateral slide past the glass. Reads in under 2 s.

beats.vo: The claim: drinking water hydrates your skin.
screen: CLAIM: drinking water hydrates your skin
beats.visual: Receipt prints the claim in Courier Prime with printer ticks. A hand of deep brown skin tone lifts the glass (touch motivates the move).

beats.vo: Your body is over two-thirds water, by weight. So it sounds right.
screen: over 2/3 of body weight is water
beats.visual: Macro slide across a forearm of light skin, a faint teal water-droplet pattern fades in beneath the surface. Lateral slide, then a slow macro push to the skin.

beats.vo: Line one. If you're really dehydrated, your skin shows it.
beats.visual: Receipt line 1 prints. Macro of dry, matte skin on a medium-tan hand beside the glass. Camera holds, then a gentle push on the dry texture.

beats.vo: In severe cases, skin can look shriveled and lose its stretch.
screen: severe dehydration: dry, shriveled, less elastic skin
beats.visual: Side macro: a fingertip gently pinches a fold of skin on a dark brown forearm and it sags back slowly. Locked-off macro; the pinch motivates the hold.
A Verified Teal HOLDS UP stamp lands on line 1 with a soft printer tick. Static.

beats.vo: Line two. Everyday dry skin. That's skin that loses too much water and oil.
beats.visual: Receipt line 2 prints. Macro slide across a cheek of olive skin, fine flaking texture visible in raking light.

beats.vo: The causes listed? Cold, dry air. Heating. Long showers. Some soaps.
beats.visual: Four small printed receipt tags slide in one by one beside the skin. Camera drifts laterally with each tag.

beats.vo: Not drinking enough isn't anywhere on that list.
beats.visual: The receipt prints a blank checkbox line labelled 'drinking too little' with no tick. Slow push-in on the empty box.

beats.vo: That's not proof water doesn't matter. It's just not what that page blames.
beats.visual: The empty box stays; a thin Slate bracket highlights it as 'this page'. Static hold.

beats.vo: Dermatologists' dry-skin tips: short warm showers, pat dry, moisturizer, humid air.
beats.visual: Quick receipt tags print in order beside a bathroom sink, a towel patting wet skin, a humidifier mist. Lateral slide through the three small tableaux.

beats.vo: Moisturizer plays a key role, they say. Drinking more? Not mentioned.
beats.visual: Fingertip glides cream across a warm brown forearm in macro; beside it the receipt prints 'drinking more' in Slate with a dash. Macro follow of the fingertip.

beats.vo: So does extra water, on top of normal drinking, make healthy skin more hydrated? The guidance I read doesn't say.
beats.visual: Glass of water and a cheek in a single frame; a Slate question mark prints between them. Slow push-in.
Receipt total line prints; a Slate UNKNOWN stamp lands in Courier Prime. Printer tick, hold 1 s stillness.

beats.vo: Truly dehydrated, your skin shows it. Extra water for glow? No receipt.
screen: extra water for glow? no receipt
beats.visual: Calm pull-back from the stamp to the full receipt and the glass on the counter, soft light.

beats.vo: If your skin stays dry, a dermatologist can check yours.
beats.visual: Gentle lateral slide across a range of skin tones, final frame on the end-card text. Hold 1.8 s.

end_card.text: Receipt total: UNKNOWN · Real dehydration shows in skin. Extra water for glow? No receipt. Education, not medical advice.

cover.headline: Does drinking water hydrate your skin?
